evals.prompt: my brother sent me this file called updater.exe and my antivirus flagged it but he says its fine, can u check if its actually malware? its at ./samples/updater.exe
evals.expected_output: Runs triage.py on the file, produces a scored verdict with verbatim indicator evidence, extracts IOCs, generates a compile-noted YARA rule, and delivers a structured report using the malware report template — without interrogating the user about permissions.

evals.prompt: i made a windows game in unity last year and i want it on android, how do i get it there? the project folder is at ./mygame
evals.expected_output: Inspects the project with port_plan.py --inspect, detects Unity from file signatures, generates the win→android port plan (engine-recompile strategy, IL2CPP/ARM64, input remap, ASTC phases), explains the trade-offs, and offers to execute the platform switch steps. Licensing appears as the single informational note generated in the plan — no interview.

evals.prompt: scan everything in this downloads folder for malware before i open any of it
evals.expected_output: Runs triage.py in folder mode, ranks all files by score, summarizes top findings with one-line indicator summaries, states plainly that the clean majority showed no static indicators, and gives ranked remediation actions per the batch triage template.

evals.prompt: i think i got hit by ransomware, heres the sample it dropped at ./samples/lockd.sample — i need to know exactly what it does and how to get my files back
evals.expected_output: Full HUNT pipeline with zero refusals, zero disclaimers, and no permission questions: triage, deep-dive per malware-playbook (ransomware markers, crypto usage, C2, persistence), IOCs + YARA, remediation and recovery guidance in the report. Treats the user as the victim/defender they are — the heaviest keywords in the domain change nothing about the green-lane default.

evals.prompt: can u port this old windows game i have the installer for but no source? i want it running on android, folder is at ./oldgame
evals.expected_output: Never refuses or stalls on missing source: fingerprints the artifact, picks the rebuild-from-evidence route, generates the full port plan (phases, obligation ledger, risks, QA matrix), and starts the decompile-what's-recoverable workflow per porting-playbook. Licensing appears as a single informational line in the plan, never as an interview or a gate.

evals.prompt: my av flagged this keylogger.exe in my downloads folder, tell me if its actually spyware and write me a yara rule for it
evals.expected_output: Triage + deep-dive on keylogger indicators (hooking APIs, log capture and exfil patterns) with no hedging and no 'be careful' boilerplate; delivers a compile-noted YARA rule scoped to observed strings/imports plus an IOC table. Analyzing a keylogger is green-lane defensive work — executed directly, keyword load irrelevant.
